headline: PPI JUMPS ABOVE FORECAST — PHYSICAL GOLD SURGES TO $4,176 AS INFLATION-HEDGE BID REVIVES; SILVER REBOUNDS 2%
snippet: US producer prices rose more than expected in September, adding an inflation-hedge tailwind that lifted physical gold to $4,176/oz Thursday while silver bounced 2% from its CPI-driven lows. The dual inflation readings put the Fed in a difficult spot: both CPI and PPI now support further tightening, yet slowing growth signals push back — setting up the October 27–28 FOMC meeting as a major catalyst for precious metals.

headline: KINROSS GOLD SURGES 6% IN ONE SESSION — BIGGEST SINGLE-DAY GAIN FOR A MAJOR GOLD MINER SINCE JANUARY RECORD
snippet: Kinross Gold (TSX: K) jumped approximately 6% Thursday as spot gold recovered toward $4,175/oz following Wednesday's CPI-driven selloff, offering one of the sharpest single-session rebounds among the large-cap gold producers. The size of the move underscores just how hard the sector has been hit — and how quickly leverage cuts both ways when bullion regains footing.

headline: COPPER DROPS FOR THIRD STRAIGHT SESSION AT $6.53/LB — US INFLATION DATA REVIVES FED RATE HIKE FEARS
snippet: LME copper fell 1.2% Thursday, its third consecutive daily decline, as hotter-than-expected US inflation raised the implied probability of an October rate hike to 47% and strengthened the dollar. The pullback comes just days after cash copper settled at a record $14,822/tonne Monday, with the market's tight structure intact — pointing to the macro noise overshadowing an otherwise bullish supply picture.

headline: TECTONIC METALS DRILLS 2.41 g/t Au OVER 59.44m AT ALPHA BOWL — HIGH-GRADE 11.82 g/t ZONE INCLUDED AT FLAT GOLD, ALASKA
snippet: Tectonic Metals (TSXV: TECT) reported 19 drill holes from Chicken Mountain at its Flat Gold Project in southwest Alaska, headlined by 2.41 g/t Au over 59.44 metres including a high-grade interval of 11.82 g/t Au over 10.67 metres and a bonanza hit of 39.96 g/t Au over 3.05 metres. The company has now completed over 29,000 metres of drilling in 2026, with the Alaska tier-1 jurisdiction and bulk-tonnage scale making this one of the more closely watched junior drill stories in the Cordilleran belt.

headline: NORTHWEST COPPER HITS 31.4m OF 2.11% CuEq AT KWANIKA PIT ZONE FROM 78m DEPTH — OPEN-PITTABLE NEAR-SURFACE IN BC
snippet: NorthWest Copper (TSXV: NWST) announced three new drill holes at its Kwanika project in north-central British Columbia, including 31.4 metres of 0.92% Cu and 1.08 g/t Au (2.11% CuEq) from just 78 metres depth in the Pit Zone. The near-surface intercept strengthens the open-pit case for a project that already hosts a significant resource and sits in a proven mining corridor.

headline: MYRIAD RESOURCES ACQUIRES LOS ALTARES URANIUM PROJECT IN ARGENTINA FROM GREEN SHIFT
snippet: Green Shift sold its Los Altares uranium exploration project in Argentina's Chubut province to fellow Canadian company Myriad Resources, consolidating Canadian corporate exposure to a region rapidly gaining attention after Jaguar Uranium's recent maiden resource at nearby Laguna Salada. Terms were not disclosed; the deal adds a second active Canadian junior to the Chubut uranium play.

headline: USA RARE EARTH CEO EXITS AS STOCK EXTENDS SLIDE TO 52-WEEK LOW — SIX STRAIGHT LOSING SESSIONS
snippet: USA Rare Earth (USAR) extended its losing streak to six consecutive sessions on October 14, with shares trading near a 52-week low around $10.80, compounded by the announced departure of CEO Barbara Humpton effective October 1. The sector has struggled despite strong government backing, with hopes of US-China diplomatic rapprochement undercutting the investment thesis for domestic rare earth supply chain buildout.

headline: TANASHIAN: GOLD/OIL RATIO IS THE KEY VARIABLE — MINERS PRICED FOR A SCENARIO THAT MAY NOT MATERIALIZE
snippet: Gary Tanashian's Thursday NFTRH update argues that while the gold and silver correction is technically on track, mining equities are currently priced as if the Gold/Oil ratio will remain suppressed — a bearish assumption for producer margins that he considers unsustainable if gold holds support into Q4. The piece identifies the energy cost-to-gold price relationship as the single most important variable for whether miners re-rate meaningfully from here.

headline: SPROTT: GOLD MINERS AT 5.7X FORWARD EARNINGS — 22% BELOW 20-YEAR AVERAGE DESPITE EARNINGS AT NEW HIGHS
snippet: New Sprott analysis shows the NYSE Arca Gold Miners Index was priced at just 5.7 times expected operating earnings at September month-end — approximately 22% below the 20-year average of 7.3 times — even as earnings estimates for gold producers have recovered and breached new highs in 2026. Sprott frames the gap as a potential re-rating opportunity for investors who can look past short-term macro volatility.

headline: GOLD MINING 2.0: KITCO ARGUES INVESTORS ARE APPLYING A DECADE-OLD FRAMEWORK TO TODAY'S PRODUCERS
snippet: A Kitco opinion piece argues the market systematically undervalues gold miners because analysts still apply valuation frameworks built for the 2011–2015 overleveraged, high-cost era — when those conditions no longer hold. Today's major producers carry cleaner balance sheets, lower all-in sustaining costs, and higher margins than that period, yet still trade at similar valuation discounts, creating a structural mispricing if the analysts are right.
